name: Red before green
claim_class: A claim that a bug fix actually fixed something.
proof_obligation: Every fix ships with a test that failed before the fix landed and passes after it, and the delivery report states plainly that this red-before-fix check was done. This is a stronger guarantee than re-running a coverage pass for each fix, because a test that already passed before the fix says nothing about whether the fix changed anything. This is distinct from the existing `induced-failure-required` record: that rule requires every robustness claim to cite an induced failure, while this rule requires every fix to carry a test that was red before the fix and green after. No hook checks this today. A hook could compare the test run before and after a fix, and until one exists this rule is carried by the prompt and by review, which is the weaker form.
failure_mode: A fix lands with a test that passed both before and after it, or with no dedicated test at all, and the report still claims the fix is proven. Nothing in the evidence shows the bug was ever reproduced, so there is no way to tell whether the change fixed the reported problem or just added an unrelated passing test next to it.
origin_incident: No single recorded event is documented for this rule. It generalizes a recurring pattern: a fix ships with a test that was never confirmed to fail on the old code, so a green suite after the fix proves nothing about whether the fix addressed the actual bug.
